treatments.name: Single-pill combination therapy
treatments.population: Adults with hypertension needing combination therapy
treatments.summary: Single-pill combinations are associated with higher adherence and persistence than free-dose combinations, but effects on blood pressure control and cardiovascular outcomes are not established.

evidence.quote: Adherence and/or persistence were generally higher in patients taking antihypertensives as SPC vs. free-dose combination; however, methodological reporting was suboptimal to facilitate comparison.
evidence.statement: Adherence and persistence were generally higher with single-pill than free-dose combinations, but reporting quality was poor.

evidence.quote: Specifically designed, well reported studies are required to determine if the increased adherence/persistence seen in patients on SPC regimen leads to improved BP control and/or cardiovascular outcomes.
evidence.statement: Whether better adherence translates into better BP control or cardiovascular outcomes still needs dedicated studies.

evidence.quote: A range of SPC therapies were studied, with calcium channel blocker/angiotensin receptor blocker combinations most common (11/29 studies).
evidence.statement: Calcium channel blocker/ARB combinations were the most studied single-pill combinations.

milestones.label: 2018 ESC/ESH guidelines call for evidence on single-pill combinations over free-dose therapy
milestones.quote: The 2018 European Society of Cardiology/European Society of Hypertension Guidelines for the management of arterial hypertension raised the need for evidence to support the use of single-pill combination (SPC) therapy in preference to free-dosed therapy for hypertension.

notes: Rapid evidence assessment: 25 of 29 included studies were observational.
